root_cause: The catalog-api v2.7.1 release added a cache warm-up that takes about 90 seconds, but the only health gate is the liveness probe (initialDelaySeconds 10, periodSeconds 10, failureThreshold 3), which starts checking 10 seconds after start and fails 3 times by ~40s because /healthz keeps returning 500 until warm-up completes. With no startupProbe, the kubelet kills every container before warm-up finishes, so the pods loop in CrashLoopBackOff and never serve traffic.
evidence: deployment.yaml: livenessProbe has initialDelaySeconds 10, periodSeconds 10, failureThreshold 3 and there is no startupProbe
catalog-api.log: cache warm-up progresses ~5% per 5s and needs ~90s, while SIGTERM arrives ~40s after each start (exit code 143)
kubectl-describe-pod.txt: Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500, followed by Killing — container failed liveness probe, will be restarted
catalog-api.log: warm-up aborts at ~35-40% on every restart, so /healthz never turns healthy
fix: Add a startupProbe to the catalog-api container (e.g. httpGet /healthz with failureThreshold 30 and periodSeconds 5) so the kubelet waits up to the warm-up window before liveness checks apply; alternatively raise the liveness probe's initialDelaySeconds above the ~90s warm-up duration. Once startup completes, the existing liveness probe takes over and pods stop restarting.
